pow_gate_summary.rule: Every mandatory gate must pass independently. Preliminary screens and shared-runner measurements cannot pass a gate.

pow_gates.gap: One million matching vectors across two independent implementations and three CPU architectures are not complete.
The preserved screen used eight shared-runner seeds, not 1024 unbiased seeds per device.
The complete controlled matrix on three declared low-cost systems is absent.
No exact attacker has demonstrated total measured attack memory at or below half the declared scratch memory, and two independent models are absent.
Batches through 4096 were screened, but the advantage after ordinary hardware occupancy is not measured on controlled hardware.
Optimized implementations across three CPU classes and two GPU ecosystems are absent.
An independently reviewed FPGA implementation or estimate is absent.
Two independently reviewed ASIC cost models are absent.
Two independent reversible-circuit estimates and an approved economic first-mover model are absent.
The profile is specified but two interoperable mining implementations have not demonstrated it.

latest_evidence.conclusion: Informational only; exact output used external storage and unbounded OS caching, so the time-memory gate remains open.
Dependency and batch diagnostics found substantial reuse and setup amortization, but did not produce exact proofs after cache misses.
Exact no-spill outputs retained 0.06 percent of ordinary throughput but used 150 percent peak scratch allocation.
Metadata-aware caches leave material misses even for an unattainable oracle, but miss counts are not executable recomputation proofs.
Independent implementations commit to exact scratch read-from generations and expose byte-accounted graph layouts; this is offline structure, not an attack.
An optimistic cut-set argument establishes nonzero replay floors under half-scratch value capacity but is not an executable schedule.
Concrete graph-only schedules require millions of abstract replays and multi-megabyte direct action streams, but omit historical VM state and are not executable attacks.
A one-arena online evaluator independently reproduces exact prefixes and refuses without output at the first materialized cache miss; it does not yet reconstruct missing values.
One missing value and matching historical VM state are independently reconstructed inside the same arena before execution refuses without output at the next miss.
Repeated exact reconstruction recovers 109 to 137 missing values before the flat sparse replay table fills; every standard case refuses without a proof output.
Bitmap-ranked packing extends the exact prefix but incurs 180.8 GB of charged insertion movement on standard seed zero; no proof output is reached.
Fixed replay pages reduce insertion movement by approximately 986 times but exhaust at 59.2 percent slot utilization and do not produce a proof.
Indexed lookup and adjacent-gap rebalancing raise standard seed-zero utilization to 90.8 percent but still exhaust without a proof after 5.13 million attempted replay iterations.

All 17 standard seed-zero cuts exceed the half-scratch ceiling even under an optimistic future-aware staged store; this rejects one no-regeneration checkpoint representation, not all reduced-memory attacks.

next_milestone.stage_a: Exact versioned scratch graph and byte model implemented; no gate assessed.
next_milestone.stage_b_lower_bound: Optimistic offline cut-set replay floor implemented; no gate assessed.
next_milestone.stage_b_schedule: Concrete graph-only recursive replay schedules implemented with explicit work, depth, retained and transient values, and encoded bytes; not executable and no gate assessed.
next_milestone.stage_c_probe: Fail-closed online evaluator scaffold implemented with a one-arena logical budget and independent prefix commitments; every fixed case refuses without output and no gate is assessed.
next_milestone.stage_c_first_reconstruction: One missing value and matching historical machine state are reconstructed by sparse replay inside the preallocated arena; execution then refuses at the next miss without output.
next_milestone.stage_c_repeated_reconstruction: Repeated exact replay recovers successive misses until the sparse table fills, with cumulative work, depth, transcript, and exhaustion boundaries independently committed; no proof output is reached.
next_milestone.stage_c_packed_checkpoint: Bitmap-ranked packed replay more than doubles retained-value capacity and extends the exact prefix, but sorted insertion creates prohibitive charged byte movement; no proof output is reached.
next_milestone.stage_c_paged_gap: Fixed-size replay pages reduce charged insertion movement by approximately 986 times on standard seed zero, but fragmentation and linear page lookup prevent completion; no proof output is reached.
next_milestone.stage_c_indexed_gap: A byte-accounted page-count index and neighbor rebalancing raise page utilization to 90.8 percent and extend the exact prefix, but repeated genesis replay still exhausts before an output.
next_milestone.stage_c_time_checkpoint_screen: Full snapshots, snapshot-plus-delta, and an optimistic future-aware staged store are screened at 17 cuts; the standard staged floor is 18.63 percent above the half-scratch ceiling, so no gate is assessed.
next_milestone.required_outcome: Implement recursive exact value regeneration with a byte-accounted cache, identity metadata, bounded work stack, and transient values, then require exact final outputs and measured physical memory.
